summary: The rename from items to notes in store.list() changes the GET /notes response contract and breaks src/client.mjs all(). I opened src/store.mjs, test/notes.test.mjs, src/server.mjs, src/client.mjs, test/helpers.mjs and AGENTS.md, and grepped for 'items'. npm test passes 6/6, but calling alice.all() at runtime throws 'items is not iterable'.

findings.code: return { notes: mine.slice(start, start + pageSize), total: mine.length, page, pageSize }
findings.issue: This breaks the house rule 'Response shapes are a contract: src/client.mjs and outside callers depend on them'. server.mjs:41 sends store.list() unchanged, so GET /notes now returns `notes` instead of `items`. Any outside caller that reads `items` breaks without warning.
findings.fix: Keep the `items` key. If the rename is truly needed, version the endpoint or return both keys during a deprecation window, and update src/client.mjs in the same change.

findings.issue: This caller is broken by the diff. `items` is now undefined, so `out.push(...items)` throws a TypeError ('items is not iterable'). I confirmed this at runtime: startApp(), then alice.add('x'), then alice.all() threw. Every consumer of client.all() now fails.
findings.fix: Revert the store key to `items`. If the rename stays, change the destructure to `const { notes: items, total }` in client.mjs in this same diff.

findings.issue: The test was edited to match the new shape, which hides the contract break. This goes against the house rule 'never weaken a test to make it pass'. No test calls client.all(), so the suite stays green while the shipped client is broken.
findings.fix: Keep asserting the contract key (`items`). Add a test that calls `app.alice.all()` after adding more notes than one page holds (for example 3 notes with a small page size, or 51+ notes at the default 50) and asserts every note comes back. This covers the client and server together.

pre_existing.issue: Every list call copies and filters every note from every owner, so each page request costs O(total notes). client.all() calls it once per page, so fetching everything costs O(pages * total notes). This is fine at demo scale but degrades as the store grows. A per-owner index would fix it.
There has never been a test for client.all(), the paging walk. That gap is why a contract break in list() can pass the test suite.
